about: TribeCode's build kit: one curated, open-source stack per kind of project, so what Flint, the AI helpers and the starters build reaches a studio-quality bar. Generated projects load these from a pinned CDN version through an import map (no install, no build step); TribeCode itself stays zero-dependency. Every library is permissively licensed (MIT, ISC, BSD, Zlib, Apache-2.0 or MPL-2.0); licenses and versions were read from the npm registry on 2026-11-10, and every pinned version is at least two weeks old. GPL pieces are left out on purpose (for example the ffmpeg.wasm core, which is GPL-2.0-or-later). 'rules' is the quality bar an AI helper checks its work against.

stacks.title: 3D game or world
stacks.what: Real-time 3D in the browser: a lit, shadowed scene with physics, controls, sound and a loading screen.

libs.name: three.js
libs.role: Renderer, scenes, glTF models, cameras, controls (addons)

libs.name: postprocessing
libs.role: Bloom-free polish: SMAA, tone mapping, vignette, depth of field

libs.name: cannon-es
libs.role: Light rigid-body physics in plain JS (the default)

libs.name: Rapier
libs.role: Fast WASM physics for many bodies, character controllers and vehicles

libs.name: three-mesh-bvh
libs.role: Fast raycasts and collisions against big meshes

libs.name: howler.js
libs.role: Sound: sprites, 3D positional audio, unlock on first tap

libs.name: lil-gui
libs.role: A tuning panel for designers (hidden behind a key)

rules: Renderer: ACESFilmic (or AgX) tone mapping, sRGB output, physically correct lights; one key light with soft shadows plus a hemisphere fill.
Hold 60 fps on a mid-range laptop and a recent phone: cap pixel ratio at 2, reuse geometries and materials, keep draw calls under ~150, use instancing for repeats.
Input feels tight: fixed-step physics (1/60 s) with interpolation, camera smoothing, pointer lock on desktop, touch sticks on phones.
A real loading screen with progress from the LoadingManager; never a black screen. Say clearly when WebGL or the CDN is unavailable.
Sound from the first interaction (unlock audio on tap/click), a mute key, and volume that ducks in menus.
Models as compressed glTF (.glb, Draco or Meshopt); textures power-of-two, KTX2 when large.
Pause when the tab is hidden; resize correctly; respect prefers-reduced-motion for camera shake.

stacks.title: 2D game
stacks.what: Crisp 2D games with scenes, sprites, tilemaps, physics and juice.

libs.name: Phaser
libs.role: Full 2D engine: scenes, arcade/matter physics, tilemaps, cameras, input

libs.name: KAPLAY
libs.role: The friendly pick for small games and game jams

libs.name: PixiJS
libs.role: The fastest 2D renderer, for custom engines and heavy effects

libs.name: matter-js
libs.role: Rigid-body 2D physics for physics toys and puzzles

libs.name: howler.js
libs.role: Sound effects and music

rules: Pixel art: integer scaling, image-rendering: pixelated, no sub-pixel camera jitter (round the camera).
Game feel: coyote time and jump buffering, hit-stop on impacts, small screen shake, particles on every important event, squash and stretch.
Fixed timestep for physics; 60 fps target with no garbage in the hot loop (pool bullets and particles).
Every action has a sound; music loops cleanly; a mute key.
Title screen, pause menu, game over and restart in one key press; controls shown on screen; touch controls on phones.
Keyboard and gamepad both work; remappable keys when there are more than four.

stacks.title: Video editor or motion
stacks.what: Edit and export video in the browser: trim, join, titles and export, with WebCodecs.

libs.name: Mediabunny
libs.role: Read, write and convert MP4/WebM with WebCodecs: decode frames, encode, mux

libs.name: wavesurfer.js
libs.role: Audio waveforms, regions and a scrubbable timeline

libs.name: Motion
libs.role: Keyframes and springs for titles and motion graphics

rules: Edit on a timeline of clips (source, in, out, track); never re-encode until Export.
Preview on a canvas at the project frame rate; scrubbing is frame-accurate and instant.
Export with WebCodecs (H.264/AAC in MP4, or VP9/Opus in WebM), with a progress bar and a Cancel button; check VideoEncoder support first and say what to use instead.
Titles are drawn on the canvas with real fonts, safe margins and a fade in/out.
Keyboard: Space play/pause, J/K/L shuttle, I/O in/out, S split, Delete removes.
Large files stay local in the browser; nothing is uploaded unless the person asks.
Leave out GPL code (the ffmpeg.wasm core is GPL-2.0-or-later); people can add it themselves if they accept that license.

stacks.title: App or tool
stacks.what: Calm, fast app screens with the tribe's palette, real icons and gentle motion.

libs.name: TribeCode design tokens
libs.role: Colors, spacing, type and radius as CSS variables (docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md)

libs.name: Lucide
libs.role: Clean, consistent icons

libs.name: Motion
libs.role: Small, purposeful transitions and springs

libs.name: Floating UI
libs.role: Menus, tooltips and popovers that stay on screen

libs.name: SortableJS
libs.role: Drag to reorder lists and boards, touch included

rules: One clear primary action per screen; a mono eyebrow and a plain title for each section.
Flat surfaces, 1px borders, depth from luminance steps only; colors from the palette variables.
Every list has an empty state that says what goes there and how to add the first one.
Keyboard reachable, visible focus rings, labels on every control, contrast at least 4.5:1.
Works at 360 px wide: thumb-sized targets (44 px), no horizontal scroll.
Motion 150–250 ms, ease-out, only for state changes; none when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
Instant feedback: optimistic updates with undo instead of confirm dialogs.

stacks.title: Website
stacks.what: Fast, accessible pages that read well and load in a blink.

libs.name: TribeCode design tokens
libs.role: Palette, type scale and spacing as CSS variables

libs.name: Lucide
libs.role: Icons

libs.name: Motion
libs.role: Scroll-linked reveals and gentle hero motion

rules: Semantic HTML first; the page works with JavaScript off.
Largest content in under 2.5 s on 4G: compressed images (WebP/AVIF) with width and height, lazy below the fold, at most two font files.
Reading layout: line-height 1.6, about 65 characters per line, a clear type scale.
One hero with one call to action; real copy, never lorem ipsum.
Meta title, description and a share image; alt text on every meaningful image.
No scroll-jacking; reveals are subtle and skipped for prefers-reduced-motion.

stacks.title: Dashboard or data
stacks.what: Charts and dashboards that are fast with real data and honest by default.

libs.name: uPlot
libs.role: Tiny, very fast time-series charts

libs.name: Chart.js
libs.role: The common chart types with good defaults

libs.name: Apache ECharts
libs.role: Big, interactive dashboards and maps

libs.name: D3
libs.role: Custom, one-of-a-kind visualizations

rules: Few numbers, big and clear; one date-range picker; the most important number first.
Bars start at zero; label axes and units; no 3D or dual axes that mislead.
One color per series, from the palette; colorblind-safe; a legend only when there are 2+ series.
Every chart has an empty state and a loading state; tooltips show exact values.
Stay smooth with 100k points (uPlot or ECharts sampling); never block the page while loading.
